name: JCaceres-R/DataJam-Turismo-Vivienda
what_it_holds: Bogotá, Colombia DataJam 2026 project pulling 7 datasets from Bogotá's open-data portal (datosabiertos.bogota.gov.co): tourist-housing (Airbnb-type) registrations, Tourist Interest Zones (ZIT) from the spatial plan, household/housing projections, municipal boundaries, cadastral valuations, tourist accommodations, and gastronomy/bar locations; raw + processed CSVs; one clustering analysis over 309 cadastral sectors; 16 commits.
why_useful: Not European, but directly on-theme for STR registration/registry data and fills LatAm gap 7 (Colombia) with an official government tourist-housing registry pull plus zoning/cadastral cross-reference — a template method transferable to the European registries.
size_hint: 7 open-data extracts, 309 cadastral sectors in one analysis
themes: European STR registration and tourist-accommodation registries (Portugal RNAL, Spain tourist dwellings, Italy CIN, France meublés de tourisme, Amsterdam, Berlin, Vienna, Lisbon, Barcelona HUTB, Paris)
why_all: Not European, but directly on-theme for STR registration/registry data and fills LatAm gap 7 (Colombia) with an official government tourist-housing registry pull plus zoning/cadastral cross-reference — a template method transferable to the European registries.

name: redfin-market-pulse
what_it_holds: Automated ETL pipeline (README.md, DAY1_GETTING_STARTED.md, .gitignore-'d data dir) that pulls U.S. real estate market data from Redfin's public 'Data Center' TSV/CSV downloads (median sale price, days on market, inventory by metro/zip). No data committed to the repo itself (data dir gitignored) -- it is a scheduled puller, not a static mirror. Small, 0 stars, very new (Apr 2026).
why_useful: Redfin Data Center covers home-price/inventory series that move with the same regional housing-cost dynamics that feed into long-term-rental supply (hosts converting owned units to STR); a working, documented client for the Redfin bulk downloads saves us from re-writing the pull ourselves, though we'd still need to run it to get an actual point-in-time file.
time_coverage: current + historical Redfin Data Center vintages (puller does not itself commit history)
size_hint: no data committed; pulls Redfin's public TSVs directly
themes: Long-term rent indices: Zillow ZORI/ZHVI downloaders, Apartment List, Redfin data center, Realtor.com, HUD Fair Market Rents, Census ACS rent, CoStar-like
why_all: Redfin Data Center covers home-price/inventory series that move with the same regional housing-cost dynamics that feed into long-term-rental supply (hosts converting owned units to STR); a working, documented client for the Redfin bulk downloads saves us from re-writing the pull ourselves, though we'd still need to run it to get an actual point-in-time file.
A ready pipeline for Redfin's own public data-center CSVs (metro/county/zip weekly-monthly housing market stats) which sit adjacent to rent and are a supply-side signal for host economics.

name: ETL-Housing-Pipeline
what_it_holds: Dockerized ETL + REST API repo (Dockerfile, README) that combines Zillow (ZHVI/ZORI-style), HUD Fair Market Rent, and Census ACS median household income data by zip code into a housing-affordability index. Contents check shows only Dockerfile/README/.gitignore at top level -- no committed CSVs, everything pulled live from the three sources at run time.
why_useful: A single working reference implementation for joining Zillow + HUD FMR + ACS by zip code; useful as a recipe/pipeline for reconstructing a long-run local rent-cost benchmark rather than as a data source itself.
time_coverage: current vintage of each source API at pipeline run time
size_hint: no data committed; Docker ETL job
themes: Long-term rent indices: Zillow ZORI/ZHVI downloaders, Apartment List, Redfin data center, Realtor.com, HUD Fair Market Rents, Census ACS rent, CoStar-like
Housing affordability and STR-housing studies data: rent-burden, vacancy, STR share of housing stock by tract
why_all: A single working reference implementation for joining Zillow + HUD FMR + ACS by zip code; useful as a recipe/pipeline for reconstructing a long-run local rent-cost benchmark rather than as a data source itself.

Zip-code-level join of Zillow rent/price index + HUD FMR + ACS income is close to a rent-burden-by-geography panel; could shortcut building our own long-term-rental cost baseline for STR<->LTR crossover work (gap #13).

name: Housing-Market-Data-Analysis (HUD API + Census ACS)
what_it_holds: Single Jupyter notebook ('Mathew Scaria - Parts1-3.ipynb', ~95KB) that calls the HUD Fair Market Rent API and Census ACS 5-Year API to build a county-level dataset (all 50 states + territories) of 2-bedroom FMR and vacancy rates, then runs OLS in R with stargazer tables. No standalone CSV committed -- the pulled table lives inside notebook cell output only.
why_useful: Working, documented calls against the HUD FMR API and ACS API for full county coverage; could be adapted to rebuild a county-level FMR/ACS-rent time series matched to Airbnb long-term-rental substitution analysis, but requires re-running the notebook to get real data out.
time_coverage: current HUD FMR + ACS 5-Year vintage at time of run
size_hint: one ~95KB notebook, no separate data files
themes: Long-term rent indices: Zillow ZORI/ZHVI downloaders, Apartment List, Redfin data center, Realtor.com, HUD Fair Market Rents, Census ACS rent, CoStar-like
why_all: Working, documented calls against the HUD FMR API and ACS API for full county coverage; could be adapted to rebuild a county-level FMR/ACS-rent time series matched to Airbnb long-term-rental substitution analysis, but requires re-running the notebook to get real data out.
Working, current one-command-ish method to combine HUD FMR + Census ACS rent/vacancy at county grain nationally — directly reusable for a host-supply-economics panel (gap 13).

name: Analysis-using-HUD-Fair-Market-Rent-Data
what_it_holds: Described as a 'lakehouse' analytics project over HUD FMR benchmarks with 'clean, interpretable datasets and visual summaries of how rents vary by geography and unit type'; not directory-inspected (budget), so committed-data status unconfirmed from description alone.
why_useful: If the lakehouse tables are actually committed (parquet/CSV under a data/ folder), this would be a ready-made structured HUD FMR panel by geography and unit type (studio/1BR/2BR/3BR/4BR), which is the standard proxy for long-term rent floors that compete with Airbnb's monthly-stay segment.
